Deputy Senate President, Senator Barau Jibrin, has commended President Bola Tinubu for his commitment to the establishment of state police, describing the Senate’s approval of the constitutional amendment bill as a historic achievement. Barau spoke on Wednesday during plenary while supporting a motion by the Senate Leader, Opeyemi Bamidele, seeking the transmission of the State Police Bill to Tinubu for assent following its approval by the required number of state Houses of Assembly. The Deputy Senate President, who chairs the Senate Committee on the Review of the 1999 Constitution, said the development marked a significant milestone in Nigeria’s efforts to decentralise its policing system and strengthen the country’s security architecture. He said successive administrations had discussed the establishment of state police and explored various options but encountered setbacks until the emergence of the Tinubu administration. Barau said, “We must, therefore, acknowledge and commend the unwavering commitment of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR, to ensuring the passage of this bill and the integration of State Police into our country’s policing architecture.” Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. State police: Senate completes amendment process, seeks Tinubu’s assent Police bust arms rings, seize grenade launcher, machine gun State police: Are our fears greater than expected benefits? “I wish to express my profound appreciation to every member of the committee on the review of the Constitution under my chairmanship, other members of the Senate and, indeed, all members of the National Assembly for their invaluable contributions to the legislative process that has brought us to this historic moment in our collective pursuit of the establishment of State Police in Nigeria. “We have all played a part in making this history,” he said. Barau urged the Senate to approve the motion without delay, noting that all the necessary legislative processes had been completed and that the remaining step was to transmit the bill to the President for assent. He explained that state police were designed to complement the operations of the Nigeria Police Force, rather than replace it, adding that the proposed arrangement would strengthen the country’s overall policing structure and improve its capacity to tackle security challenges. “The remaining step is to transmit the bill to Mr President for his assent,” he said. Barau also congratulated members of the National Assembly and other stakeholders who contributed to the constitutional amendment process.
